name: Kaspr
description: Kaspr is a business-contact enrichment platform that uses standard LinkedIn profile URLs to return names, professional and direct email addresses, phone numbers, job titles, company information and other profile data.
agentUseSummary: Kaspr documents a customer-owned API-key integration for credit-consuming contact enrichment, but its public reference does not publish the required v2 header name, current dataToGet values, complete request and response schemas, error contract or plan limits. Relay cannot publish Connect or expose personal-data tools until Kaspr supplies a pinned current contract and approves Relay's bounded use.

capabilities.label: Read a bounded business profile
capabilities.description: After provider review, enrich exactly one standard LinkedIn profile URL with the minimum licensed professional fields through a pinned schema and reduced response.

blocked.label: Connect before contract review
blocked.description: No Kaspr key, connection or request may be accepted until Kaspr supplies the current v2 header, dataToGet enum, complete request and response schemas, errors, limits, credits, rotation, revocation, retention and authorized AI-processing contract.

blocked.label: Block platform credentials and LinkedIn automation
blocked.description: Kaspr usernames, passwords, shared accounts, LinkedIn sessions, Sales Navigator URLs, cookies, extensions, browser or mobile automation, scraping, copied tokens and reverse-engineered endpoints are unavailable as API substitutes.

blocked.label: Block personal contact data and consequential use
blocked.description: Direct or personal email, personal or mobile phone, home or precise location, sensitive data, identity decisions, employment screening, eligibility decisions, automated outreach, spam and other consequential uses are unavailable.

blocked.label: Block bulk, export, redistribution, and raw access
blocked.description: CSV or file upload, contact lists, bulk enrichment, retries, pagination, CRM sync, arbitrary dataToGet values, raw responses, caching, model training, resale, sublicensing, public or third-party redistribution, raw API, browser, CLI and unrestricted access are unavailable.

approvalProfiles.label: Kaspr API review pending
approvalProfiles.description: All actions remain unavailable until Kaspr approves Relay's use, publishes or supplies a pinned current API contract, and the customer authorizes the applicable personal-data, credit, retention and lawful-purpose boundaries.

runtimeSupport.description: A pinned one-profile business-data wrapper can be mounted after provider and legal review; no OpenClaw tool is callable while review is pending.
A pinned one-profile business-data wrapper can be mounted after provider and legal review; no Hermes tool is callable while review is pending.

providerSetup.blocker: Kaspr's current help article documents POST https://api.developers.kaspr.io/profile/linkedin with an Authorization API key and JSON body, but its sample contains only name and id while the troubleshooting section says working requests must specify v2 in an unnamed header and include dataToGet fields. The linked public Stoplight reference currently exposes only an introduction and no operation schema. Public materials do not establish the v2 header name, dataToGet enum, complete request or response schemas, error bodies, per-plan hourly and daily limits, safe retry behavior, key rotation or revocation, or a Relay-specific AI-processing contract. Each successful request consumes an export credit and requested email or phone credits even for repeat contacts; the API returns personal data retained in Kaspr's database for up to five years and governed by opt-out and lawful-purpose duties. Relay will not invent a schema, accept a broad key, disclose personal contact data, or spend customer credits without explicit authority.
providerSetup.nextAction: Kaspr and a customer sponsor must confirm that Relay may act as the customer's server-side API client; provide the current version header, dataToGet values, pinned request and response schemas, errors, plan limits, credit accounting, key issue/rotation/revocation and test tenant; and approve exact professional fields, lawful purpose, data-subject rights, source notice, storage, retention, deletion, AI processing, audit, internal users and redistribution boundaries. After review, implement only a single standard LinkedIn-profile enrichment wrapper, default to professional identity and B2B email fields, require per-call approval because credits and personal data are involved, reject Sales Navigator and every bulk or raw surface, reduce output, disable retries and persistence, and verify credit use, schema drift denial, rotation, revocation and post-disconnect denial.

evidence.supports: Kaspr markets LinkedIn-profile enrichment for names, email addresses, phone numbers, job titles and company information; states that API access starts on a paid plan; and charges field-specific credits plus one export credit per successful call.

Kaspr documents API-key authorization and POST /profile/linkedin, rejects Sales Navigator URLs, charges repeated contacts again, prohibits resale, and separately says a v2 header and dataToGet fields are required without naming or defining them.

Kaspr's linked public API reference identifies the project but currently exposes only an introduction, not the operation, authentication, request, response, error, limit or revocation schemas needed for a pinned connector.

Kaspr's terms limit use to professional users and subscriptions, define B2B email, phone, direct email and export credits, require confidential account credentials, protect the contact database, prohibit unsolicited bulk messages and restrict substantial extraction, reuse and resale.

Kaspr describes business-profile names, emails, phones, social URLs, employers, titles and locations; its public and partner sources, customer purposes, legitimate-interest basis, opt-out rights, recipients, transfers and retention for up to five years.

Kaspr states that it relies on legitimate interest subject to a balancing test, data-protection impact assessment, transparent notice and data-subject access rights rather than treating API access as blanket authority for every use.
